claim: The ZeroLink Git history places nopara73's initial repository work on 2017-07-28, before any Samourai-attributed contribution, and shows a substantive wallet-privacy framework already present before the first Samourai commit.
subject: ZeroLink authorship chronology
supporting_excerpt: Initial commit
caveat: Authorship is inferred from the full chronology and document content, not commit count alone; later contributions and prior influences are not erased by this finding.

claim: The first SamouraiDev/TDevD commit to ZeroLink was dated 2017-07-30 and was a typo-only patch titled 'Fix typos.'
subject: SamouraiDev's first ZeroLink contribution
supporting_excerpt: Subject: [PATCH] Fix typos
caveat: This characterizes the first commit only; it does not claim there were no later technical contributions.

claim: Wasabi's published architecture used Tor and client-side block-filter checks so its backend did not receive a wallet xpub, while blinded coordination was designed to prevent the coordinator from linking registered inputs to outputs.
subject: Wasabi Wallet operator-privacy architecture
supporting_excerpt: The Wasabi indexer (backend) sends a block filter of all the transactions in each block to all the clients. Then, users check locally
caveat: The archive establishes the documented design and threat model, not flawless implementation against every adversary or in every release; the date is the archive retrieval date.

claim: In the production Android source snapshot immediately preceding the October 2022 xpub dispute, absence of Dojo selected Samourai's hosted backend, and the API path sent joined xpubs to the selected backend.
subject: Samourai Android hosted-backend xpub path
supporting_excerpt: // use samourai backend
caveat: This is an exact cited snapshot, not a claim about every historical release; an xpub cannot spend funds but can reveal the derived wallet graph.

claim: Samourai Android v0.99.95 treated Tor as disabled unless the user enabled it and used a non-Tor request path for xpub queries when Tor was not required.
subject: Samourai Android Tor default
supporting_excerpt: getValue(PrefsUtil.ENABLE_TOR, false)
caveat: The finding is limited to the cited signed-source snapshot and the paths examined; Tor support existed and could be enabled.

claim: Samourai GitLab issue #458 documented a wallet-creation screen with Tor off and Dojo unconfigured, proposed safer defaults or warnings, and was closed on the day it was filed.
subject: GitLab issue 458 privacy-default report
supporting_excerpt: Important privacy features are disabled by default
caveat: The issue and screenshot establish the shown defaults, proposal, response, and closure; they do not independently establish how many users retained those settings.

claim: Dojo server code was announced on 2019-06-02, but wallet pairing arrived on 2019-07-11 and initially supported newly created wallets while restoration of an existing wallet was unsupported.
subject: Dojo release and initial pairing limitation
supporting_excerpt: Restoring your existing wallet with Dojo is currently unsupported
caveat: This concerns initial availability; later versions may have removed the limitation, but later pairing could not retract an xpub already disclosed.

claim: Sentinel commit 77eca1d moved XPUB multiaddr lookups from Blockchain.info to the Samourai API on 2017-08-12.
subject: Sentinel xpub routing
supporting_excerpt: APIFactory: move XPUB multiaddr to Samourai API
caveat: The commit establishes the endpoint move; it does not imply that an xpub permits spending funds.

claim: Sentinel added Tor routing and a network dashboard on 2019-09-20, more than two years after moving xpub requests to Samourai's API.
subject: Sentinel Tor support chronology
supporting_excerpt: [ADDED] Network Dashboard, Support for tor routing in network code
caveat: Later source still made Tor a user choice; this claim does not say Tor was unavailable after this date.

claim: On 2022-10-03 the official Samourai Wallet account called the Android product a full-node wallet, although the cited production source selected a backing server and sent xpub requests when Dojo was absent.
subject: Samourai 'full node wallet' claim
supporting_excerpt: We are a full node wallet. Always have been.
caveat: A user-run Dojo could place the backend on the user's full node; the narrow contradiction concerns the default Android app without Dojo.

claim: When a user said xpubs were sent to Whirlpool servers, Hill's @SamouraiDev reply denied that the coordinator handled xpubs, leaving the separate Samourai wallet-backend path unaddressed.
subject: Hill's coordinator-versus-backend xpub reply
supporting_excerpt: No xpubs are handled by the coordinator.
caveat: The quoted sentence is narrowly true of the coordinator/backend distinction; the essay's criticism is that it did not answer whether a separate hosted backend received xpubs.

claim: The surviving Blockchain.info Android repository is dominated by William Hill-attributed commits, and focused file comparisons show clear lineage from that client into Samourai's first published source snapshot.
subject: Blockchain.info Android to Samourai source lineage
supporting_excerpt: The repository begins with William Hill's April 30, 2014
caveat: The audit does not claim Hill or Rodriguez founded Blockchain.info, nor that the entire Samourai codebase was a verbatim fork.

claim: Samourai publicly announced on 2017-12-21 that it had finalized the acquisition of OXT in an all-bitcoin transaction and described it as a long-term strategic investment.
subject: Samourai acquisition of OXT
supporting_excerpt: Samourai has finalized the acquisition
caveat: The announcement also said OXT would remain a separate entity operated by its existing team; later filings use the stronger phrase 'owned and operated.'
essay_section: The OXT “critical vulnerability” that failed its own test

claim: OXT's 2020 Wasabi analysis required an observer to know the target wallet's composition at a chosen step and related mixing events; its demonstration gave Eve knowledge of Alice's funds and used a modified client to log rounds.
subject: OXT Wasabi-report assumptions
supporting_excerpt: composition of the targeted wallet at a given step N
caveat: The report may still describe useful hardening concerns; this claim is limited to what its tested model assumes and does not prove the absence of every related attack.
essay_section: The OXT “critical vulnerability” that failed its own test

claim: Bitcoin Optech publicly described the WabiSabi protocol on 2020-06-17, before OXT's August 2020 disclosure, contradicting the chronology that Wasabi 2 began as a reaction to that disclosure.
subject: WabiSabi development chronology
supporting_excerpt: WabiSabi coordinated coinjoins with arbitrary output values
caveat: Prior public work disproves a simple origin story but does not show that later engineering choices were wholly uninfluenced by criticism.
essay_section: The OXT “critical vulnerability” that failed its own test

claim: The reproducible Dumplings dataset records 247,675.31 fresh BTC entering Wasabi and 30,228.14 entering Whirlpool from April 2019 through August 2022, with Wasabi higher in all 41 shared months.
subject: Wasabi and Whirlpool fresh-bitcoin volume
supporting_excerpt: Wasabi's fresh-bitcoin volume was 8.19 times Whirlpool's
caveat: Fresh BTC is an on-chain volume proxy, not a count of users, installations, wallets, or people.
essay_section: The megaphone was bigger than the product

claim: Samourai's own 2021 statement referred to Whirlpool TX0 output as unmixed 'toxic change,' showing that isolating change outside the CoinJoin did not make it disappear from transaction history.
subject: Whirlpool TX0 toxic change
supporting_excerpt: unmixed “toxic change” from Whirlpool CoinJoin transactions
caveat: TX0 can reduce accidental co-spending and keeps change out of the CoinJoin transaction; the claim is only that the change remains linkable in the broader history.
essay_section: Moving the problem did not solve it

claim: The cited Samourai Android Ricochet source set four hops by default and constructed a sequential chain in which each hop spent the preceding transaction.
subject: Ricochet transaction-chain shape
supporting_excerpt: public final static int defaultNbHops = 4;
caveat: A recognizable construction is not proof that any particular user was deanonymized; the essay expressly limits the claim to the source-visible pattern.
essay_section: Moving the problem did not solve it

claim: The 2021 PIN-bypass disclosure showed that restarting the Samourai app reset its in-memory failed-attempt counter, enabling repeated PIN trials against copied device data; the issue was cataloged as CVE-2021-36689.
subject: Samourai Wallet PIN authentication bypass
supporting_excerpt: To bypass the 3 PIN attempts we can simply restart the application and the counter will reset.
caveat: This is a local/offline attack requiring access to wallet data, not evidence of a remote universal wallet-draining vulnerability.

claim: The journalist who had characterized nopara73 as admitting that Wasabi CoinJoined with users publicly corrected the account and said nopara73 had made no such statement in their direct messages.
subject: Correction of Wasabi-liquidity allegation
supporting_excerpt: He never said in our DMs that @wasabiwallet CoinJoins with users.
caveat: This corrects the reporter's characterization; it does not independently establish every fact about Wasabi liquidity.

claim: After a categorical April 2023 assertion that Whirlpool already changed Tor circuits between registration phases, a March 2024 client commit added changeIdentity() immediately before output registration with an unlinking comment.
subject: Whirlpool Tor identity change
supporting_excerpt: // use new identity to unlink from input
caveat: The later patch does not prove earlier rounds were deanonymized, exploited, or wholly unprotected; it establishes that the categorical earlier answer was not safely supported by the later code history.

claim: nopara73's published sockpuppet investigation attributed the 'foneBTC' and 'fone-btc' accounts to TDevD/William Hill using account, project, and Soft Machines links.
subject: foneBTC and fone-btc attribution
supporting_excerpt: This is conclusive evidence that fone-btc and TDevD are the same person.
caveat: This is the author's evidence-based attribution, not an independent adjudication or platform identity disclosure; the alias file preserves the uncertainty explicitly.

claim: The official @SamouraiWallet account posted 'Snitches get stitches' on 2023-04-18 during the public conflict.
subject: Official Samourai Wallet threat-coded post
supporting_excerpt: Snitches get stitches
caveat: The record establishes the project account's words and timing, not which individual typed the post or a specific plan to commit violence.

claim: On 2023-04-20 @SamouraiDev told nopara73 he deserved 'much worse' and paired the text with an image of armed men surrounding a captive.
subject: @SamouraiDev April 2023 image post
supporting_excerpt: As a die hard collaborator, you deserve much worse.
caveat: The source establishes the text and attached image; describing the combination as a threat is the recipient's interpretation rather than a judicial finding.

claim: A preserved 2026-07-10 @SamouraiDev profile snapshot named nopara73, used 'gutted' language, and displayed the small town where nopara73 says his parents live.
subject: @SamouraiDev profile doxxing context
supporting_excerpt: It ain't over until the fat boy is gutted

claim: U.S. authorities announced that Icelandic law enforcement seized Samourai's web servers and domain on 2024-04-24.
subject: Samourai server and domain seizure
supporting_excerpt: In coordination with law enforcement authorities in Iceland, Samourai’s web servers and domain (https://samourai.io/) were seized.
caveat: The seizure is a procedural fact; the arrest announcement's criminal accusations were allegations at that stage, not verdicts.

claim: The government's 2025 sentencing memorandum represented that retained mobile-user xpub data could, through complex cross-referencing, connect inputs and outputs for many Whirlpool transactions, while expressly stating that this did not itself identify real-world users.
subject: Government xpub server-analysis representation
supporting_excerpt: retained sufficient information to trace or “demix” its mobile users’ Whirlpool transactions
caveat: Confidence is high that the filing makes this representation; the underlying forensic work was not independently published, and the filing says the analysis did not itself deanonymize users.

claim: The same government filing quotes Hill, after the seizure, writing 'Not good' and expressing greater concern about 'the wallet backends (xpubs)' than Whirlpool.
subject: Hill post-seizure xpub message
supporting_excerpt: I'm not thinking so much about Whirlpool as I am about the wallet backends (xpubs).
caveat: The filing supplies the quote and context; the archive does not contain the underlying message export, and concern alone does not prove malicious use of the data.

claim: Hill's sentencing submission acknowledged xpub collection for light-wallet balance calculation and asserted that it affected 'only 20%' of Whirlpool users.
subject: Defense xpub and 20-percent assertion
supporting_excerpt: This affected only 20% of Whirlpool users
caveat: Confidence is high that the defense made the statement, but only medium in the percentage itself because the filing gives no source, method, counts, or independent validation.

claim: A 2023 archived GitLab report identified a Whirlpool coordinator-fee address reused in 37 transactions; an archived transaction record shows one cited consolidation spent 36 outputs previously sent to that address.
subject: Whirlpool coordinator-fee address reuse
supporting_excerpt: the coordinator has been reusing receive addresses in some instances to collect this fee
caveat: Address reuse alone does not prove Whirlpool users were demixed; the claim that the issue was later deleted rests on the reporter's same-day account, not a later Wayback capture.

claim: The 2025 superseding indictment alleged that Hill promoted Whirlpool on Dread to users openly discussing criminal proceeds and that Rodriguez knew Hill was performing promotional work there.
subject: Dread marketing allegations
supporting_excerpt: Samourai Whirlpool is a much better option
caveat: Confidence is high only that the indictment made the allegation; an indictment is not a finding. Later guilty pleas are indexed separately and should not be read as admission of every pleaded allegation.

claim: Rodriguez and Hill each pleaded guilty on 2025-07-30 to one count of conspiracy to operate a money-transmitting business knowing that it transmitted crime proceeds.
subject: Rodriguez and Hill guilty pleas
supporting_excerpt: each pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to operate a money transmitting business knowing the business transmitted crime proceeds
caveat: The Justice Department announced the pleas on 2025-08-06; the plea date stated in the release is 2025-07-30. The money-laundering-conspiracy count was dropped under the plea agreements.

claim: Rodriguez was sentenced to five years in prison on 2025-11-06 and Hill to four years on 2025-11-19.
subject: Rodriguez and Hill sentences
supporting_excerpt: RODRIGUEZ and HILL were respectively sentenced to five and four years in prison.
caveat: The sentences resolve the criminal cases under the pleas; they do not adjudicate the essay's separate software-authorship, privacy-architecture, or interpersonal claims.
